title.zh: 卷八十二 王商史丹傅喜傳
title.en: Volume 82: Wang Shang, Shi Dan and Fu Xi
title.raw: 卷八十二 王商史丹傅喜傳 Volume 82: Wang Shang, Shi Dan and Fu Xi

sentences.zh: 卷八十二 王商史丹傅喜傳第五十二

translations.literal: Volume 82: Biographies of Wang Shang, Shi Dan, and Fu Xi, Number 52.
translations.idiomatic: Volume 82: Biographies of Wang Shang, Shi Dan, and Fu Xi (the fifty-second chapter).

sentences.zh: 王商字子威，涿郡蠡吾人也，徙杜陵。

translations.literal: Wang Shang, courtesy name Ziwei, was a man of Liwu in Zhuo Commandery, and his family moved to Duling.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shang, whose courtesy name was Ziwei, came from Liwu in Zhuo Commandery; the household later relocated to Duling.

sentences.zh: 商公武、武兄無故，皆以宣帝舅封。

translations.literal: Shang's father was Wu; Wu's elder brother was Wugu; both were enfeoffed because they were uncles on the mother's side of Emperor Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shang's father was Wang Wu, and Wu's elder brother Wang Wugu; both received marquisates as maternal uncles of Emperor Xuan.

sentences.zh: 無故為平昌侯，武為樂昌侯。

translations.literal: Wugu became Marquis of Pingchang, and Wu became Marquis of Lechang.
translations.idiomatic: Wugu was made Marquis of Pingchang, while Wu became Marquis of Lechang.

sentences.zh: 語在《外戚傳》。

translations.literal: The account is in the 'Biographies of the Consort Families.'
translations.idiomatic: The fuller story appears in the chapter on the imperial in-laws.

sentences.zh: 商少爲太子中庶子，以肅敬敦厚稱。

translations.literal: When young, Shang served as palace attendant to the heir and was known for solemn respect and solid integrity.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Wang Shang served as palace attendant to the crown prince and was known for solemn respect and steadfast integrity.

sentences.zh: 父薨，商嗣爲侯，推財以分異母諸弟，身無所受，居喪哀戚。

translations.literal: When his father died, Shang succeeded as marquis, pushed out wealth to divide among half-brothers by a different mother, himself received nothing, and in mourning was grief-stricken.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, Wang Shang inherited the marquisate, gave away his share of the estate to his half-brothers, kept nothing for himself, and mourned with deep grief.

sentences.zh: 於是大臣薦商行可以厲群臣，義足以厚風俗，宜備近臣。

translations.literal: Thereupon great ministers recommended Shang, saying his conduct could sharpen the host of officials and his righteousness was sufficient to enrich custom; he should be prepared as a close minister.
translations.idiomatic: Senior ministers then recommended him, saying his conduct could set an example for the bureaucracy and his righteousness could strengthen public morals; he ought to serve close to the throne.

sentences.zh: 繇是擢爲諸曹、侍中、中郎將。

translations.literal: From this he was promoted to the various bureaus, palace attendant, and leader of the palace gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore promoted to posts in the various bureaus, as palace attendant, and as leader of the palace gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 元帝時，至右將軍、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In Emperor Yuan's time he reached General of the Right and Grand Master of the Household.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Yuan he rose to General of the Right and Grand Master of the Household.

sentences.zh: 是時，定陶共王愛幸，幾代太子。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Gong of Dingtao was loved and favored and nearly replaced the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Prince Kang of Dingtao enjoyed the emperor's favor and nearly displaced the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 商爲外戚重臣輔政，擁佑太子，頗有力焉。

translations.literal: Shang, as a weighty minister among the consort kin assisting government, supported and protected the heir apparent and had considerable force therein.
translations.idiomatic: As a leading consort-clan minister in the government, Wang Shang supported the crown prince and did much to protect his position.

sentences.zh: 元帝崩，成帝即位，甚敬重商，徙為左將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan died, Emperor Cheng ascended the throne; he greatly respected Wang Shang and transferred him to be General of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Yuan died and Emperor Cheng took the throne, the new sovereign held Wang Shang in high regard and appointed him General of the Left.

sentences.zh: 而帝元舅大司馬大將軍王鳳顓權，行多驕僭。

translations.literal: But the emperor's eldest uncle on the mother's side, Grand Marshal and Grand General Wang Feng, monopolized power, and his conduct was often arrogant and presumptuous.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Wang Feng, the emperor's senior maternal uncle, served as grand marshal and grand general and dominated the government, and his behavior was frequently overbearing and out of line.

sentences.zh: 商論議不能平鳳，鳳知之，亦疏商。

translations.literal: In deliberations Shang could not restrain Feng; Feng knew it and also kept Shang at a distance.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shang could not curb Wang Feng in council debate; Feng noticed the friction and kept his distance from him.

sentences.zh: 建始三年秋，京師民無故相驚，言大水至，百姓奔走相蹂躪、老弱號呼，長安中大亂。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the third year of the Jianshi era, the people of the capital for no reason frightened one another, saying great floodwaters were coming; the common people ran about, trampling one another, the old and weak cried out, and great chaos arose in Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Jianshi 3, rumor swept the capital that a catastrophic flood was imminent; people panicked, stampeded, and trampled one another while the elderly and children wailed, and Chang'an descended into chaos.

sentences.zh: 天子親御前殿，召公卿議。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven personally went to the front hall and summoned the dukes and ministers to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went in person to the front hall and called the high ministers into council.

sentences.zh: 大將軍鳳以為太后與上及後宮可御船，令吏民上長安城以避水。

translations.literal: Grand General Feng thought the empress dowager, the sovereign, and the rear palace could board boats, and ordered clerks and people to ascend the walls of Chang'an to escape the water.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Feng proposed putting the empress dowager, the emperor, and the harem aboard boats and ordering officials and townsfolk onto the ramparts of Chang'an to ride out the supposed flood.

sentences.zh: 群臣皆從鳳議。

translations.literal: The host of ministers all followed Feng's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The entire court fell in behind Wang Feng's plan.

sentences.zh: 左將軍商獨曰：「自古無道之國，水猶不冒城郭。

translations.literal: General of the Left Shang alone said, 'Since antiquity, even in states without the Way, floodwaters have not overrun city walls.
translations.idiomatic: Only General of the Left Wang Shang objected: 'Since antiquity, even in states without the Way, floodwaters have not overrun city walls.

sentences.zh: 今政治和平，世無兵革，上下相安，何因當有大水一日暴至？

translations.literal: Now government and policies are peaceful, the age has no warfare, high and low are at ease with one another—what reason could there be for great waters suddenly to arrive in a single day?
translations.idiomatic: We live in a time of peace, without war, and ruler and ruled are secure together; what could cause a deluge to strike the capital in an instant?

sentences.zh: 此必訛言也，不宜令上城，重驚百姓。」

translations.literal: This must be false rumor; it is not fitting to order people onto the walls and again frighten the hundred surnames.'
translations.idiomatic: This is surely a groundless scare. Ordering everyone onto the walls would only panic the populace again.'

sentences.zh: 上乃止。

translations.literal: The sovereign thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dropped the idea.

sentences.zh: 有頃，長安中稍定，問之，果訛言。

translations.literal: After a while, within Chang'an things gradually settled; when it was investigated, it was indeed false rumor.
translations.idiomatic: Before long calm returned to Chang'an, and inquiries confirmed that the alarm had been nothing but rumor.

sentences.zh: 上於是美壯商之固守，數稱其議。

translations.literal: The sovereign thereupon praised and admired Shang's steadfast holding firm, and repeatedly commended his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then praised Wang Shang for holding firm and repeatedly commended his counsel.

sentences.zh: 而鳳大慚，自恨失言。

translations.literal: But Feng was greatly ashamed and hated himself for having misspoken.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Feng was deeply embarrassed and bitterly regretted his rash words.

sentences.zh: 明年，商代匡衡為丞相，益封千戶，天子甚尊任之。

translations.literal: The next year, Shang replaced Kuang Heng as chancellor; his fief was increased by a thousand households, and the Son of Heaven greatly honored and employed him.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Wang Shang succeeded Kuang Heng as chancellor, received an additional thousand-household grant to his estate, and enjoyed the emperor's full confidence.

sentences.zh: 為人多質有威重，長八尺餘，身體鴻大，容貌甚過絕人。

translations.literal: As a person he was much of substance and possessed awe-inspiring dignity; he was more than eight chi in height, his body was vast, and his appearance greatly surpassed other men.
translations.idiomatic: He was plainspoken yet imposing—well over eight feet tall, with a massive frame and a face that towered above ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 河平四年，單于來朝，引見白虎殿。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of the Heping era, the Chanyu came to court and was led in audience at the White Tiger Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In Heping 4 the Xiongnu chanyu paid a formal visit, and the court received him in the White Tiger Hall.

sentences.zh: 丞相商坐未央廷中，單于前，拜謁商。

translations.literal: Chancellor Shang sat in the Weiyang court; the Chanyu advanced and bowed in audience to Shang.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Wang Shang took his seat in the Weiyang Palace court; the chanyu stepped forward and performed obeisance to him.

sentences.zh: 商起，離席與言，單于仰視商貌，大畏之，遷延卻退。

translations.literal: Shang rose, left his mat, and spoke with him; the Chanyu looked up at Shang's appearance, greatly feared him, and hesitatingly drew back.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shang stood, stepped from his place, and addressed him; when the chanyu lifted his eyes to Wang Shang's towering figure, he shrank back in awe and edged away.

sentences.zh: 天子聞而歎曰：「此真漢相矣！」

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven heard and sighed, saying, 'This is truly a Han chancellor!'
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of it, he sighed and said, 'This truly is a Han chancellor!'

sentences.zh: 初，大將軍鳳連昏楊肜為琅邪太守，其郡有災害十四，已上。

translations.literal: Earlier, Grand General Feng had allied by marriage with Yang Rong, who served as governor of Langye; that commandery had fourteen or more disasters.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Feng had earlier formed a marriage alliance with Yang Rong, governor of Langye, a commandery that had suffered more than a dozen calamities.

sentences.zh: 商部屬按問，鳳以曉商曰：「災異天事，非人力所為。

translations.literal: Shang's subordinate officials investigated; Feng used it to inform Shang, saying, 'Disasters and prodigies are affairs of Heaven, not what human power does.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shang ordered his staff to look into the matter. Wang Feng sent word: 'Portents come from Heaven; no mortal official controls them.

sentences.zh: 肜素善吏，宜以為後。」

translations.literal: Rong has always been a capable official; he should be treated leniently in this matter.'
translations.idiomatic: Yang Rong has always been capable in office; you ought to deal with this leniently.'

sentences.zh: 商不聽，竟奏免肜，奏果寢不下，鳳重以是怨商，陰求其短，使人上書言商閨門內事。

translations.literal: Shang did not listen; in the end he memorialized to dismiss Rong; the memorial indeed lay asleep and was not issued; Feng for this reason again resented Shang, secretly sought his shortcomings, and caused someone to submit a memorial speaking of affairs inside Shang's women's quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shang ignored the hint, memorialized for Yang Rong's removal, and saw the document shelved. Wang Feng's resentment deepened; he began hunting for dirt and had someone memorialize about scandal inside Wang Shang's household.

sentences.zh: 天子以為暗昧之過，不足以傷大臣，鳳固爭，下其事司隸。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven thought obscure faults were not sufficient to injure a great minister; Feng firmly disputed, and the matter was sent down to the metropolitan commandant.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor treated the charges as private indiscretions unworthy of ruining a senior minister, but Wang Feng pressed the case until the matter was referred to the metropolitan superintendent.

sentences.zh: 先是，皇太后嘗詔問商女，欲以備後宮。

translations.literal: Before this, the empress dowager had once issued an edict inquiring about Shang's daughter, wishing to prepare her for the rear palace.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the empress dowager had formally inquired after Wang Shang's daughter with an eye to admitting her to the harem.

sentences.zh: 時女病，商意亦難之，以病對，不入。

translations.literal: At that time the daughter was ill; Shang in his mind also found it difficult; he answered with illness, and she did not enter.
translations.idiomatic: The girl happened to be ill, and Wang Shang himself was reluctant; he pleaded sickness, and she never entered the palace.

sentences.zh: 及商以閨門事見考，自知為鳳所中，惶怖，更欲內女為援，乃因新幸李婕妤家白見其女。

translations.literal: When Shang because of women's-quarters matters underwent examination, he knew himself to have been struck by Feng; frightened, he further wished to send in a daughter as support; then through the household of the newly favored Lady Li, Jieyu, he reported and showed his daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wang Shang faced investigation over domestic scandal, he realized Wang Feng had set him up. In panic he tried to push his daughter into the palace as a counterweight and used the household of the newly favored Lady Li to present her.

sentences.zh: 會日有蝕之，太中大夫蜀郡張匡，其人佞巧，上書願對近臣陳日蝕咎。

translations.literal: It happened that there was a solar eclipse; Grand Master of the Palace Zhang Kuang of Shu commandery, a man crafty and sycophantic, submitted a memorial wishing to address close ministers and explain the eclipse's blame.
translations.idiomatic: When a solar eclipse occurred, Palace Grandee Zhang Kuang of Shu commandery, a sly and fawning man, submitted a memorial asking to address the emperor's close advisers on the meaning of the eclipse.

sentences.zh: 下朝者左將軍丹等問匡，對曰：「竊見丞相商作威作福，從外制中，取必於上，性殘賊不仁，遣票輕吏微求人罪，欲以立威，天下患苦之。

translations.literal: When the court adjourned, General of the Left Dan and others questioned Kuang; he replied: "I have privately seen Chancellor Shang making authority and making favor, controlling the center from outside, taking what he must from above; his nature is cruel, predatory, and without humaneness; he sends swift light clerks to probe subtly for people's crimes, wishing thereby to establish awe; all under heaven suffer and are pained by it.
translations.idiomatic: After court, General of the Left Shi Dan and others questioned Zhang Kuang. He answered, "I have observed Chancellor Wang Shang wielding arbitrary power, controlling the court from outside, and extracting whatever he wants from the throne. He is cruel and ruthless, sending out swift minor officials to hunt for crimes in order to terrify the realm, and the people suffer greatly under him.

sentences.zh: 前頻陽耿定上書言商與父傅通，及女弟淫亂，奴殺其私夫，疑商教使。

translations.literal: Earlier Geng Ding of Pinyang submitted a memorial saying Shang had illicit relations with his father's concubine, and that his younger sister's conduct was licentious—a slave killed her paramour, and there was suspicion Shang instructed and sent him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Geng Ding of Pinyang memorialized that Wang Shang had slept with his father's concubine, that his younger sister was promiscuous, and that a slave had killed her lover—some suspected Wang Shang had ordered it.

sentences.zh: 章下有司，商私怨懟。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down to the proper offices; Shang privately harbored resentment and defiance.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the proper offices, and Wang Shang nursed private resentment.

sentences.zh: 商子俊欲上書告商，俊妻左將軍丹女，持其書以示丹，丹惡其父子乘迕，爲女求去。

translations.literal: Shang's son Jun wished to submit a memorial accusing Shang; Jun's wife was General of the Left Dan's daughter; she took the memorial and showed it to Dan; Dan hated the father and son's mutual defiance and sought divorce for his daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shang's son Jun tried to memorialize against his father. Jun's wife was Shi Dan's daughter; she showed the draft to her father. Dan despised the father-and-son breach and sought a divorce for his daughter.

sentences.zh: 商不盡忠納善以輔至德，知聖主崇孝，遠別不親，後庭之事皆受命皇太后，太后前聞商有女，欲以備後宮，商言有固疾，後有耿定事，更詭道因李貴人家內女，執左道以亂政，誣罔悖大臣節，故應是而日蝕。

translations.literal: Shang does not exhaust loyalty and accept goodness to assist utmost virtue; knowing the sage sovereign honors filial piety and that distant partings are not intimate, rear-palace affairs all receive command from the empress dowager—the empress dowager earlier heard Shang had a daughter and wished to prepare her for the rear palace; Shang said she had a chronic illness; later came the Geng Ding affair, and further by devious paths through the household of the newly favored Lady Li he sought to send in a daughter; he holds to the left path and disorders government, deceives and violates a great minister's integrity—therefore Heaven responded with a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shang has not served with full loyalty or accepted good counsel to support your supreme virtue. Knowing that a sage ruler honors filial piety and that the empress dowager governs the inner palace, he refused when the empress dowager earlier asked for his daughter for the harem, pleading chronic illness. After the Geng Ding affair he tried again through the household of the newly favored Lady Li to smuggle a daughter inside. He practices heterodox ways that corrupt government and violates every standard of a chief minister—hence the eclipse.

sentences.zh: 《周書》曰：『以左道事君者誅。』

translations.literal: The Documents of Zhou says: "Those who serve the ruler by the left path are executed."
translations.idiomatic: The Documents of Zhou says, "Those who serve their ruler by heterodox means are put to death."

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：『日中見昧，則折其右肱。』

translations.literal: The Changes says: "When gloom appears at midday, break the right upper arm."
translations.idiomatic: The Changes says, "When darkness appears at noon, break the right arm."

sentences.zh: 往者丞相周勃再建大功，及孝文時纖介怨恨，而日爲之蝕，於是退勃使就國，卒無怵惕憂。

translations.literal: In the past Chancellor Zhou Bo twice established great merit; when in Emperor Wen's time there were minute resentments, the sun was eclipsed for it; then Bo was dismissed and sent to his state, and in the end had no fearful worry.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Chancellor Zhou Bo had rendered great service twice, yet when minor resentments arose under Emperor Wen the sun was eclipsed on his account; the emperor then sent Bo back to his fief, and he lived out his days without further fear.

sentences.zh: 今商無尺寸之功，而有三世之寵，身位三公，宗族爲列侯、吏二千石、侍中諸曹，給事禁門內，連昏諸侯王，權寵至盛。

translations.literal: Now Shang has not a sliver of merit, yet enjoys three generations of favor; his person ranks among the Three Excellencies; his clan are ranked marquises, officials of two thousand shi, palace attendants and bureau officials, serving inside the forbidden gates; he has allied by marriage with feudal lords and kings—power and favor reach the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Today Wang Shang has achieved nothing, yet enjoys three generations of imperial favor. He holds one of the Three Excellencies; his clan fills marquisates, two-thousand-shi offices, palace attendance, and bureau posts inside the forbidden gates; his family is intermarried with kings and lords, and his power and favor are at their height.

sentences.zh: 審有內亂殺人怨懟之端，宜究竟考問。

translations.literal: Truly there are beginnings of inner disorder, murder, resentment, and defiance; he should be fully investigated and questioned.
translations.idiomatic: There are clear signs of domestic scandal, murder, and defiance; the matter should be thoroughly investigated.

sentences.zh: 臣聞秦丞相呂不韋見王無子，意欲有秦國，即求好女以爲妻，陰知其有身而獻之王，產始皇帝。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that Qin chancellor Lü Buwei, seeing the king had no son, wished to possess the state of Qin; he then sought a fine woman as wife, secretly knowing she was with child and presenting her to the king, and she bore the First Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that Qin's chancellor Lü Buwei, seeing that the king had no heir, plotted to seize Qin: he found a beautiful woman, knew she was pregnant, and presented her to the king, and she bore the First Emperor.

sentences.zh: 及楚相春申君亦見王無子，心利楚國，即獻有身妻而產懷王。

translations.literal: And Chu chancellor Lord Chunshen likewise saw the king had no son, his heart set on benefiting the state of Chu; he then presented a pregnant wife and she bore King Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Chu's chancellor Lord Chunshen did the same when he saw the king had no heir, scheming for Chu's advantage by presenting a pregnant wife who bore King Huai of Chu.

sentences.zh: 自漢興幾遭呂、霍之患，今商有不仁之性，乃因怨以內女，其奸謀未可測度。

translations.literal: Since Han rose, the dynasty has nearly suffered the calamities of the Lü and Huo clans; now Shang has an unkind nature and, because of resentment, seeks to send in a daughter—his treacherous plot cannot be measured.
translations.idiomatic: Since the founding of Han the dynasty has nearly fallen to the Lü and Huo clans. Wang Shang is ruthless and, nursing grievance, now tries to place a daughter in the palace—who can gauge the depth of such treachery?

sentences.zh: 前孝景世七國反，將軍周亞夫以爲即得雒陽劇孟，關東非漢之有。

translations.literal: Formerly in Emperor Jing's time the seven states rebelled; General Zhou Yafu thought that if one obtained Ju Meng of Luoyang, the lands east of the Pass would not belong to Han.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Jing's reign the seven states rebelled. General Zhou Yafu said that with Ju Meng of Luoyang on their side, the rebels could take everything east of the Pass from Han.

sentences.zh: 今商宗族權勢，合貲巨萬計，私奴以千數，非特劇孟匹夫之徒也。

translations.literal: Now Shang's clan in power and influence together possess wealth reckoned in tens of thousands; private slaves number in the thousands—they are not merely the likes of Ju Meng, a common man.
translations.idiomatic: Today Wang Shang's clan commands wealth beyond counting and keeps thousands of private slaves—they are far more dangerous than a lone adventurer like Ju Meng.

sentences.zh: 且失道之至，親戚畔之，閨門內亂，父子相訐，而欲使之宜明聖化，調和海內，豈不謬哉！

translations.literal: Moreover, when one reaches the extreme of losing the Way, kin turn against one, the women's quarters are in inner disorder, father and son accuse each other—and yet one wishes to make him clarify and spread sage transformation and harmonize the realm within the seas: is this not absurd!
translations.idiomatic: When a man has lost the Way so completely that kin rebel, the household is in scandal, and father and son denounce each other, how can he be expected to embody sage rule and harmonize the empire? The very idea is absurd!

sentences.zh: 商視事五年，官職陵夷而大惡著於百姓，甚虧損盛德，有鼎折足之凶。

translations.literal: Shang has held office five years; official duties have declined while great evil is manifest among the hundred surnames, greatly damaging and diminishing august virtue—there is the omen of a tripod with a broken leg.
translations.idiomatic: In five years in office Wang Shang has let government decay while the people suffer openly, gravely harming your sacred virtue—the omen of a broken tripod leg.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以爲聖主富於春秋，即位以來，未有懲奸之威，加以繼嗣未立，大異並見，尤宜誅討不忠，以遏未然。

translations.literal: Your foolish servant thinks the sage sovereign is rich in years of spring and autumn; since ascending the throne there has not been awe in punishing the treacherous; moreover the succession is not yet established and great prodigies appear together—it is especially fitting to execute and attack the disloyal to check what is not yet happened.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant believes that although Your Majesty is still young, since your accession you have not yet shown decisive power against traitors. With the succession unsettled and great portents appearing together, this is the moment to punish disloyalty and forestall worse to come.

sentences.zh: 行之一人，則海內震動，百奸之路塞矣。」

translations.literal: Act against one man, and the realm within the seas will be shaken; the paths of a hundred treacheries will be blocked."
translations.idiomatic: Strike down this one man, and the empire will tremble; the roads of every kind of treachery will be closed."

sentences.zh: 於是左將軍丹等奏：「商位三公，爵列侯，親受詔策為天下師，不遵法度以翼國家，而回辟下媚以進其私，執左道以亂政，為臣不忠，罔上不道，《甫刑》之辟，皆為上戮，罪名明白。

translations.literal: Thereupon General of the Left Dan and others submitted: 'Shang occupies the Three Excellencies, his noble rank is marquis; he personally received edicts and appointments as teacher to all under heaven; he does not follow laws and regulations in order to wing the state, but turns aside and flatters those below to advance his private interests, holds to the left path and disorders government; as a minister he is disloyal, deceives the sovereign and is not in accord with the Way; the punishments of the Fu Xing are all capital executions for superiors—his guilt is clear.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Left Shi Dan and his colleagues then memorialized: 'Wang Shang ranks among the Three Excellencies and holds a marquisate; he was personally commissioned to guide the realm. Instead of upholding the law to support the state, he courts favor below and pursues private ends, peddling heterodox practices that corrupt government. Such disloyalty and deceit of the throne violate the standards of the Fu Xing and merit execution; his offenses are plain.

sentences.zh: 臣請詔謁者召商詣若盧詔獄。」

translations.literal: We request that an edict be issued to the usher summoning Shang to the Rolu imperial prison.'
translations.idiomatic: We ask that Your Majesty order the court usher to take Wang Shang into custody at the Rolu imperial prison.'

sentences.zh: 上素重商，知匡言多險，制曰「勿治」。

translations.literal: The sovereign had always esteemed Shang; he knew Kuang's words were mostly treacherous, and issued a rescript saying, 'Do not prosecute.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had long respected Wang Shang and recognized Zhang Kuang's memorial for the vicious attack it was, so he ruled, 'Take no further action.'

sentences.zh: 鳳固爭之，於是制詔御史：「蓋丞相以德輔翼國家，典領百寮，協和萬國，為職任莫重焉。

translations.literal: Feng firmly disputed it; thereupon an edict was issued to the imperial secretary: 'In general the chancellor with virtue assists and wings the state, presides over the host of officials, harmonizes the myriad states—of offices and duties none is heavier.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Feng would not let the matter drop, and the emperor had to issue an edict to the censor-in-chief: 'The chancellor exists to support the dynasty with moral authority, to head the bureaucracy, and to keep the realm in harmony—no burden is weightier.

sentences.zh: 今樂昌侯商為丞相，出入五年，未聞忠言嘉謀，而有不忠執左道之辜，陷於大辟。

translations.literal: Now Lechang Marquis Shang has been chancellor, going in and out five years; loyal words and fine plans have not been heard from him, yet there is the guilt of disloyalty and holding to the left path, falling into great execution.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in five years as chancellor, Lechang Marquis Wang Shang has offered no loyal counsel worthy of the name, while the charge of disloyalty and heterodox conduct would carry the death penalty.

sentences.zh: 前商女弟內行不修，奴賊殺人，疑商教使，為商重臣，故抑而不窮。

translations.literal: Earlier Shang's younger sister's conduct within was not cultivated; a slave villainously killed a person; there was suspicion Shang instructed and sent him; because Shang was a weighty minister, therefore it was suppressed and not fully investigated.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier his younger sister's private conduct was scandalous: a household slave committed murder, and some suspected Wang Shang ordered it. Because he was a pillar of the court, I suppressed the case and did not press to the bottom.

sentences.zh: 今或言商不以自悔而反怨懟，朕甚傷之。

translations.literal: Now some say Shang does not thereby repent himself but instead harbors resentment; We are greatly wounded by it.
translations.idiomatic: Now I am told he shows no remorse but nurses grievance instead. That wounds me deeply.

sentences.zh: 惟商與先帝有外親，未忍致於理。

translations.literal: Only, Shang has outer kinship with the late emperor; We have not been able to bear bringing him to the law.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Wang Shang is tied to the late emperor by marriage, and I cannot bring myself to subject him to full criminal process.

sentences.zh: 其赦商罪。

translations.literal: Let Shang's crimes be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore pardon his offenses.

sentences.zh: 使者收丞相印綬。」

translations.literal: Let envoys collect the chancellor's seal and ribbon.'
translations.idiomatic: Envoys shall relieve him of the chancellor's seal and sash.'

sentences.zh: 商免相三日，發病嘔血薨，謚曰戾侯。

translations.literal: Three days after Shang was removed as chancellor, he fell ill, vomited blood, and died; his posthumous title was Marquis Li.
translations.idiomatic: Three days after Wang Shang was dismissed as chancellor, he fell ill, vomited blood, and died. He was posthumously titled Marquis Li.

sentences.zh: 而商子弟親屬爲駙馬都尉、侍中、中常侍、諸曹大夫郎吏者，皆出補吏，莫得留給事宿衛者。

translations.literal: And Shang's sons, younger brothers, and kin who were chief commandants of horsemen-at-attendance, palace attendants, palace secretaries, bureau grand masters, and clerks and gentlemen—all were sent out to fill outside posts and none were allowed to remain serving in attendance or palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: All of Wang Shang's sons, brothers, and kinsmen who held posts as chief commandant of horsemen-at-attendance, palace attendant, palace secretary, bureau official, or clerk were reassigned to outside offices and none were allowed to remain on palace duty or in the guard.

sentences.zh: 有司奏商罪過未決，請除國邑。

translations.literal: The proper offices memorialized that Shang's crimes and faults were not yet settled and requested abolition of the state and fief.
translations.idiomatic: The proper offices reported that Wang Shang's offenses were still unresolved and asked that his fief be abolished.

sentences.zh: 有詔長子安嗣爵爲樂昌侯，至長樂衛尉、光祿勳。

translations.literal: There was an edict that the eldest son An should succeed to the title as Marquis of Lechang, reaching the posts of Commandant of Chang'le Palace Guard and Superintendent of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that his eldest son Wang An inherit the title as Marquis of Lechang; he later rose to Commandant of the Chang'le Palace Guard and Superintendent of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 商死後，連年日蝕、地震，直臣京兆尹王章上封事召開，訟商忠直無罪，言鳳顓權蔽主。

translations.literal: After Shang died, year after year there were solar eclipses and earthquakes; the upright official metropolitan governor Wang Zhang submitted a sealed memorial; when summoned, it was opened, and he argued that Shang was loyal and straight and without guilt, saying Feng monopolized power and blocked the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Shang's death, solar eclipses and earthquakes followed year on year. Wang Zhang, the principled governor of the capital, submitted a sealed memorial; when the emperor summoned him and opened it, Zhang argued that Wang Shang had been loyal and blameless and that Wang Feng had monopolized power and blinded the throne.

sentences.zh: 鳳竟以法誅章，語在《元後傳》。

translations.literal: Feng in the end by law executed Zhang; the account is in the 'Biography of the Yuan Empress Dowager.'
translations.idiomatic: Wang Feng eventually had Wang Zhang executed on a legal pretext; the story is told in the biography of Empress Dowager Yuan.

sentences.zh: 至元始中，王莽為安漢公，誅不附己者，樂昌侯安見被以罪，自殺，國除。

translations.literal: By the Yuanshi era, Wang Mang was Duke of Anhan; he executed those who did not attach to himself; Lechang Marquis An was seen to be charged with crime, killed himself, and the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanshi years Wang Mang, as Duke of Anhan, purged everyone who would not bend to him. Lechang Marquis Wang An was framed, took his own life, and his marquisate was extinguished.

sentences.zh: 史丹字君仲，魯國人也，徙杜陵。

translations.literal: Shi Dan, courtesy name Junzhong, was a man of Lu state; his family moved to Duling.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Dan, courtesy name Junzhong, came from Lu; his family later relocated to Duling.

sentences.zh: 祖父恭有女弟，武帝時爲衞太子良娣，產悼皇考。

translations.literal: His grandfather Gong had a younger sister who in Emperor Wu's time was a worthy lady attendant to the Heir of Wei, the crown prince, and bore the Lamented Imperial Father.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shi Gong had a younger sister who, in Emperor Wu's reign, served as a worthy lady attendant to Crown Prince Wei and bore the Lamented Imperial Father.

sentences.zh: 皇考者，孝宣帝父也。

translations.literal: The Imperial Father was the father of Emperor Xuan of Filial Piety.
translations.idiomatic: The Lamented Imperial Father was Emperor Xuan's father.

sentences.zh: 宣帝微時依倚史氏。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan was in humble circumstances he relied on the Shi clan.
translations.idiomatic: In his lowly days Emperor Xuan relied on the Shi family.

sentences.zh: 語在《史良娣傳》。

translations.literal: The account is in the "Biography of Worthy Lady Attendant Shi."
translations.idiomatic: The fuller account appears in the biography of Lady Attendant Shi.

sentences.zh: 及宣帝即尊位，恭已死，三子，高、曾、玄。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan assumed the exalted throne, Gong was already dead; he had three sons: Gao, Zeng, and Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan took the throne, Gong was already dead, leaving three sons: Gao, Zeng, and Xuan.

sentences.zh: 曾、玄皆以外屬舊恩封：曾爲將陵侯，玄平台侯。

translations.literal: Zeng and Xuan were both enfeoffed for old favor as outer kin: Zeng became Marquis of Jiangling, Xuan Marquis of Pingtai.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng and Xuan were both enfeoffed as maternal relatives on account of old favor: Zeng as Marquis of Jiangling and Xuan as Marquis of Pingtai.

sentences.zh: 高侍中，貴幸，以發舉反者大司馬霍禹功封樂陵侯。

translations.literal: Gao was palace attendant, honored and favored; for exposing and reporting the rebel Grand Marshal Huo Yu he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yueling.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Gao served as palace attendant and enjoyed high favor; for exposing the rebel Grand Marshal Huo Yu he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yueling.

sentences.zh: 宣帝疾病，拜高爲大司馬、車騎將軍，領尚書事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan was ill, Gao was appointed Grand Marshal and General of Chariots and Cavalry, overseeing Masters of Writing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan fell ill, he appointed Shi Gao Grand Marshal and General of Chariots and Cavalry with oversight of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 帝崩，太子襲尊號，是爲孝元帝。

translations.literal: The emperor died; the heir apparent assumed the exalted title—this was Emperor Yuan of Filial Piety.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died, the crown prince succeeded as Emperor Yuan.

sentences.zh: 高輔政五年，乞骸骨，賜安車駟馬、黃金，罷就第。

translations.literal: Gao assisted government five years, begged for his old bones, was granted a secure carriage and four horses and gold, was dismissed, and went to his mansion.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Gao served as regent for five years, then asked to retire. He was given a comfortable carriage and team of four, gold, and permission to withdraw to his estate.

sentences.zh: 薨，謚曰安侯。

translations.literal: He died; his posthumous title was Marquis An.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously titled Marquis An.

sentences.zh: 自元帝為太子時，丹以父高任為中庶子，侍從十餘年。

translations.literal: From the time when Emperor Yuan was heir apparent, Dan, through his father Shi Gao's rank, was appointed palace attendant to the heir and attended him for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Yuan was still crown prince, Shi Dan, through his father Shi Gao's standing, was appointed palace attendant to the heir and served at his side for more than a decade.

sentences.zh: 元帝即位，為駙馬都尉侍中，出常驂乘，甚有寵。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan ascended the throne, he became chief commandant of horsemen-at-attendance and palace attendant; when going out he often rode in the accompanying chariot; he had great favor.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan took the throne, Shi Dan became chief commandant of horsemen-at-attendance and palace attendant, routinely rode beside the emperor in the side car, and basked in imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 上以丹舊臣，皇考外屬，親信之，詔丹護太子家。

translations.literal: The sovereign because Dan was an old minister and outer kin of the imperial father trusted him closely, and issued an edict for Dan to guard the heir apparent's household.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor treated Shi Dan as a veteran of his father's household and a maternal relative, kept him close, and ordered him to oversee the crown prince's establishment.

sentences.zh: 是時，傅昭儀子定陶共王有材藝，子母俱愛幸，而太子頗有酒色之失，母王皇后無寵。

translations.literal: At this time, Consort Fu's son the Prince of Dingtao, the Prince of Gong, had talent and arts; son and mother were both loved and favored, while the heir apparent had quite failings of wine and sex, and his mother Empress Wang had no favor.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Consort Fu's son, Prince Kang of Dingtao, was gifted and accomplished, and mother and son both enjoyed the emperor's affection, whereas the crown prince showed a weakness for wine and women and his mother, Empress Wang, had fallen out of favor.

sentences.zh: 建昭之後，元帝被疾，不親政事，留好音樂。

translations.literal: After the Jianzhao era, Emperor Yuan was afflicted with illness, did not personally handle government affairs, and lingered in love of music.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jianzhao period Emperor Yuan fell ill, ceased to attend to government himself, and devoted himself to music.

sentences.zh: 或置鼙鼓殿下，天子自臨軒檻上，隤銅丸以擿鼓，聲中嚴鼓之節。

translations.literal: Sometimes side drums were set below the hall; the Son of Heaven himself stood on the balustrade above, dropped copper balls to strike the drums, and the sound hit the cadence of the ceremonial drums.
translations.idiomatic: Drums were sometimes set below the hall; the emperor himself stood on the upper balustrade, dropped copper balls to beat the drums, and matched the rhythm of the ceremonial drum pattern.

sentences.zh: 後宮及左右習知音者莫能爲，而定陶王亦能之，上數稱其材。

translations.literal: Those in the rear palace and at the sovereign's side practiced in knowing music yet none could do it; but the Prince of Dingtao could also do it, and the sovereign repeatedly praised his talent.
translations.idiomatic: None of the harem or the emperor's attendants who knew music could match the feat, yet the Prince of Dingtao could, and the emperor repeatedly praised his ability.

sentences.zh: 丹進曰：「凡所謂材者，敏而好學，溫故知新，皇太了是也。

translations.literal: Dan advanced and said: "What is called talent is quickness and love of learning, warming the old and knowing the new—the heir apparent is such.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Dan stepped forward and said, "True talent means quickness and love of learning, reviewing the old to know the new—the crown prince is such a man.

sentences.zh: 若乃器人於絲竹鼓鼙之間，則是陳惠、李微高於匡衡，可相國也。」

translations.literal: If one gauges men amid strings, bamboo, drums, and side drums, then Chen Hui and Li Wei are higher than Kuang Heng and could be chancellor of the state."
translations.idiomatic: If you measure men by skill with music and drums, then Chen Hui and Li Wei outrank Kuang Heng and ought to be chancellor."

sentences.zh: 於是上嘿然而笑。

translations.literal: Thereupon the sovereign gave a silent laugh.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor smiled but said nothing.

sentences.zh: 其後，中山哀王薨，太子前吊。

translations.literal: After this the Prince Ai of Zhongshan died; the heir apparent went forward to mourn.
translations.idiomatic: Later Prince Ai of Zhongshan died, and the crown prince went to offer condolences.

sentences.zh: 哀王者，帝之少弟，與太子遊學相長大。

translations.literal: Prince Ai was the emperor's younger brother; he and the heir apparent studied and traveled together and grew up together.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ai was the emperor's younger brother; he and the crown prince had studied and grown up together.

sentences.zh: 上望見太子，感念哀王，悲不能自止。

translations.literal: The sovereign looked and saw the heir apparent, was moved by thoughts of Prince Ai, and grieved beyond self-control.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor saw the crown prince, memories of Prince Ai overwhelmed him and he could not stop grieving.

sentences.zh: 太子既至前，不哀。

translations.literal: When the heir apparent had come forward, he did not mourn.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince came forward, he showed no grief.

sentences.zh: 上大恨曰：「安有人不慈仁而可奉宗廟爲民父母者乎！」

translations.literal: The sovereign greatly resented it and said: "How can there be a man lacking kindness and humaneness who can be entrusted with the ancestral temple and be father and mother to the people!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and said, "How can anyone lacking kindness and humaneness be fit to tend the ancestral temple and be father and mother to the people!"

sentences.zh: 上以責謂丹。

translations.literal: The sovereign blamed and addressed Dan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reproached Shi Dan.

sentences.zh: 丹免冠謝上曰：「臣誠見陛下哀痛中山王，至以感損。

translations.literal: Dan removed his cap and apologized to the sovereign, saying: "Your servant truly saw Your Majesty grieving for the Prince of Zhongshan, even to the point of being moved and harmed.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Dan removed his cap and apologized: "Your servant saw that Your Majesty was grieving for Prince Ai of Zhongshan to the point of harming your health.

sentences.zh: 向者太子當進見，臣竊戒屬毋涕泣，感傷陛下。

translations.literal: When the heir apparent was about to come forward in audience, your servant privately admonished and instructed him not to weep and cry, lest he move and wound Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince was about to appear, I privately warned him not to weep and add to Your Majesty's sorrow.

sentences.zh: 罪乃在臣，當死。」

translations.literal: The crime lies in your servant; I deserve death."
translations.idiomatic: The fault is mine alone, and I deserve death."

sentences.zh: 上以爲然，意乃解。

translations.literal: The sovereign thought it so; his resentment then dissolved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted this explanation and his anger subsided.

sentences.zh: 丹之輔相，皆此類也。

translations.literal: Dan's assisting and guiding the heir were all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Dan's guidance of the crown prince was always of this sort.

sentences.zh: 竟寧元年，上寢疾，傅昭儀及定陶王常在左右，而皇后、太子希得進見。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingning the sovereign lay ill; Consort Fu and the Prince of Dingtao were constantly at his side, while the empress and heir apparent seldom obtained audience.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingning 1 the emperor was bedridden. Consort Fu and the Prince of Dingtao were constantly at his side, while the empress and crown prince were rarely admitted.

sentences.zh: 上疾稍侵，意忽忽不平，數問尚書以景帝時立膠東王故事。

translations.literal: The sovereign's illness gradually worsened; his mind was unsettled and uneasy; he repeatedly questioned the Masters of Writing about the precedent of Emperor Jing's time in establishing the Prince of Jiaodong.
translations.idiomatic: As his illness deepened, the emperor grew restless and repeatedly asked the Masters of Writing about the precedent from Emperor Jing's reign of enthroning the Prince of Jiaodong instead of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 是時，太子長舅陽平侯王鳳爲衛尉、侍中，與皇后、太子皆憂，不知所出。

translations.literal: At this time the heir apparent's elder maternal uncle, Yangping Marquis Wang Feng, was Commandant of the Guard and palace attendant; he together with the empress and heir apparent were all worried and did not know what course to take.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's elder maternal uncle, Yangping Marquis Wang Feng, served as Commandant of the Guard and palace attendant; he, the empress, and the crown prince were all anxious and at a loss.

sentences.zh: 丹以親密臣得侍視疾，侯上間獨寢時，丹直入臥內，頓首伏青蒲上，涕泣言曰：「皇太子以適長立，積十餘年，名號繫於百姓，天下莫不歸心臣子。

translations.literal: Dan, as an intimate minister, was allowed to attend and view the illness; waiting until the sovereign was alone at rest, Dan went straight into the sleeping quarters, knocked his head and lay prostrate on the green rush mat, and with tears said: "The heir apparent was established as eldest son of the primary consort and has accumulated more than ten years; his title is tied to the hundred surnames; all under heaven none do not turn their hearts to him as lord and son.
translations.idiomatic: As an intimate adviser permitted to attend the sickbed, Shi Dan waited until the emperor was resting alone, then entered the inner chamber, prostrated himself on the green rush mat, and weeping said, "The crown prince was established as the legitimate eldest son more than ten years ago. His title is bound up with the people, and all the realm looks to him as heir.

sentences.zh: 見定陶王雅素愛幸，今者道路流言，爲國生意，以爲太子有動搖之議。

translations.literal: Seeing the Prince of Dingtao has long been loved and favored, now there are rumors on the roads; the state is stirred; people think there is talk of shaking the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Dingtao has long enjoyed your favor, and now rumor runs through the streets that the succession may be changed.

sentences.zh: 審若此，公卿以下必以死爭，不奉詔。

translations.literal: If this is truly so, from the dukes and ministers downward they will surely contend unto death and not obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: If that is true, the high ministers and officials below them will resist to the death and refuse to obey any contrary edict.

sentences.zh: 臣願先賜死以示群臣！」

translations.literal: Your servant wishes first to be granted death to show the host of ministers!"
translations.idiomatic: Your servant asks to die first as a warning to the court!"

sentences.zh: 天子素仁，不忍見丹涕泣，言又切至，上意大感，喟然太息曰：「吾日困劣，而太子、兩王幼少，意中戀戀，亦何不念乎！

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven was by nature humane; he could not bear to see Dan weeping; his words were also urgent and penetrating; the sovereign was greatly moved, sighed deeply, and said: "My days are weary and weak, yet the heir apparent and the two princes are young and small; my heart is attached and lingering—how could I not think of them!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was by nature humane and could not bear to see Shi Dan weeping. His words cut to the heart. Deeply moved, the emperor sighed and said, "My days are failing, and the crown prince and the two princes are still young. My heart clings to them—how could I not think of them!

sentences.zh: 然無有此議。

translations.literal: Yet there is no such deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: But there is no such plan.

sentences.zh: 且皇后謹慎，先帝又愛太子，吾豈可違指！

translations.literal: Moreover the empress is careful and cautious; the former emperor also loved the heir apparent—how could I go against his intent!
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the empress is prudent, and the late emperor loved the crown prince. How could I go against his intent!

sentences.zh: 駙馬都尉安所受此語？」

translations.literal: Chief Commandant of Horsemen-at-attendance, from where did you receive these words?"
translations.idiomatic: Chief Commandant of Horsemen-at-attendance, where did you hear such talk?"

sentences.zh: 丹即卻，頓首曰：「愚臣妾聞，罪當死！」

translations.literal: Dan at once withdrew and knocked his head, saying: "Your foolish servant and concubine-subject heard it; the crime deserves death!"
translations.idiomatic: Shi Dan drew back and kowtowed: "This foolish servant merely heard rumor. The offense deserves death!"

sentences.zh: 上因納，謂丹曰：「吾病浸加，恐不能自還。

translations.literal: The sovereign thereupon accepted it and said to Dan: "My illness is gradually increasing; I fear I cannot return on my own.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted this and said to Shi Dan, "My illness grows worse, and I fear I may not recover.

sentences.zh: 善輔道太子，毋違我意！」

translations.literal: Well assist and guide the heir apparent; do not go against my intent!"
translations.idiomatic: Guide the crown prince well and do not betray my intent!"

sentences.zh: 丹噓唏而起。

translations.literal: Dan sobbed and rose.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Dan sobbed and rose.

sentences.zh: 太子由是遂爲嗣矣。

translations.literal: The heir apparent thereby became the successor.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince was thereby secured as successor.

sentences.zh: 元帝竟崩，成帝初即位，擢丹爲長樂衛尉，遷右將軍，賜爵關內侯，食邑三百戶，給事中，後徙左將軍、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan finally died; when Emperor Cheng first ascended the throne, Dan was promoted to Commandant of the Chang'le Palace Guard, transferred to General of the Right, granted rank as Marquis within the Pass with a fief of three hundred households, given palace attendance, and later moved to General of the Left and Grand Master of the Household.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan died and Emperor Cheng first succeeded, Shi Dan was promoted to Commandant of the Chang'le Palace Guard, then General of the Right, granted Marquis within the Pass with a three-hundred-household fief and palace attendance, and later moved to General of the Left and Grand Master of the Household.

sentences.zh: 鴻嘉元年，上遂下詔曰：「夫褒有德，賞元功，古今通義也。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongjia the sovereign then issued an edict saying: "To praise those with virtue and reward primary merit is the common principle of antiquity and the present.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongjia 1 the emperor issued an edict: "Honoring the virtuous and rewarding great service is a principle honored in every age.

sentences.zh: 左將軍丹往時導朕以忠正，秉義醇一，舊德茂焉。

translations.literal: General of the Left Dan in former times guided Us with loyalty and uprightness, held righteousness pure and single, and old virtue flourished therein.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Left Shi Dan long ago guided Us with loyal uprightness, held to pure integrity, and his old merit is abundant.

sentences.zh: 其封丹爲武陽侯，國東海郯之武強聚，戶千一百。」

translations.literal: Let Dan be enfeoffed as Marquis of Wuyang, with his state at Wuqiang village in Tan of Donghai, one thousand one hundred households."
translations.idiomatic: Let Shi Dan be enfeoffed as Marquis of Wuyang, with a fief at Wuqiang in Tan county, Donghai commandery, of eleven hundred households."

sentences.zh: 丹為人足知，愷弟愛人，貌若儻蕩不備，然心甚謹密，故尤得信於上。

translations.literal: Dan as a person was sufficient in knowledge, kindly and fraternal, loving people; his appearance seemed careless and unprepared, yet his heart was very careful and secret; therefore he especially obtained trust from the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Dan was shrewd, warm, and considerate; he looked relaxed and even careless, but he was meticulous by nature, which is why the emperor trusted him above others.

sentences.zh: 丹兄嗣父爵為侯，讓不受分。

translations.literal: Dan's elder brother inherited their father's marquisate as marquis; Dan yielded and did not accept a share.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother inherited their father's marquisate; Shi Dan declined any share of the estate.

sentences.zh: 丹盡得父財，身又食大國邑，重以舊恩，數見褒賞，賞賜累千金，僮奴以百數，後房妻妾數十人，內奢淫，好飲酒，極滋味聲色之樂。

translations.literal: Dan completely obtained the father's wealth; his person moreover ate a great state's fief; doubled with old favor, he repeatedly received praise and rewards; rewards and gifts accumulated to a thousand pounds of gold; household slaves were in the hundreds; rear chambers had wives and concubines in the tens of persons; within he was extravagant and dissolute, fond of drinking wine, and exhausted the pleasures of flavors, sounds, and sex.
translations.idiomatic: He kept the whole of his father's fortune, drew income from a large fief, and, thanks to long-standing favor, was heaped with honors and gifts worth thousands in gold. He kept hundreds of slaves, dozens of concubines, and lived in private luxury—drinking heavily and indulging every appetite for food, music, and women.

sentences.zh: 為將軍前後十六年，永始中病乞骸骨，上賜策曰：「左將軍寢病不衰，願歸治疾，朕愍以官職之事久留將軍，使躬不瘳。

translations.literal: Serving as general before and after sixteen years, in the Yongshi era he was ill and begged for his bones; the sovereign bestowed a rescript saying: 'General of the Left, your lying illness does not wane; you wish to return to treat illness; We pity that the affairs of office have long detained the general, causing your person not to recover.
translations.idiomatic: He served sixteen years as a general. In the Yongshi period he fell ill and asked to retire. The emperor replied: 'Your illness as General of the Left does not improve, and you wish to go home to heal. I regret that state business has kept you at your post so long that your health has not mended.

sentences.zh: 使光祿勳賜將軍黃金五十斤，安車駟馬，其上將軍印綬。

translations.literal: Let the superintendent of the imperial household be sent to bestow on the general fifty jin of gold, a secure carriage and four horses; let him present the general's seal and ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: Send the superintendent of the imperial household with fifty catties of gold, a comfortable carriage and team of four, and take your seal and sash as general.

sentences.zh: 宜專精神，務近醫藥，以輔不衰。」

translations.literal: You should concentrate spirit, devote yourself to drawing near to physicians and medicine, in order to assist non-declining.'
translations.idiomatic: Devote yourself to rest and medical care so that your strength may return.'

sentences.zh: 丹歸第數月薨，謚曰頃侯。

translations.literal: Several months after Dan returned to his mansion he died; his posthumous title was Marquis Qing.
translations.idiomatic: A few months after Shi Dan retired to his estate he died and was posthumously titled Marquis Qing.

sentences.zh: 有子男女二十人，九男皆以丹任並爲侍中、諸曹，親近在左右。

translations.literal: He had twenty sons and daughters; nine sons all through Dan's appointment together became palace attendants and bureau officials, close and near at the sovereign's side.
translations.idiomatic: He had twenty children; nine sons, through Shi Dan's influence, all held posts as palace attendants and bureau officials close to the throne.

sentences.zh: 史氏凡四人侯，至卿、大夫、二千石者十餘人，皆訖王莽乃絶，唯將陵侯曾無子，絶於身云。

translations.literal: Among the Shi clan four men in all were marquises; those reaching ministers, grand masters, and two-thousand-shi rank numbered more than ten—all ended only when Wang Mang came, except Jiangling Marquis Zeng, who had no son and ended in his own person.
translations.idiomatic: Four members of the Shi clan became marquises, and more than a dozen reached ministerial or two-thousand-shi rank; the line ended only under Wang Mang, except Marquis of Jiangling Zeng, who died without heirs.

sentences.zh: 傅喜字稚游，河內溫人也，哀帝祖母定陶傅太后從父弟。

translations.literal: Fu Xi, courtesy name Zhiyou, was a man of Wen in Henei; he was the younger brother by the same father of Empress Dowager Fu of Dingtao, Emperor Ai's grandmother.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xi, courtesy name Zhiyou, came from Wen in Henei commandery. He was the younger brother of Grand Empress Dowager Fu of Dingtao, Emperor Ai's grandmother.

sentences.zh: 少好學問，有志行。

translations.literal: From youth he loved learning and inquiry and had purpose in conduct.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved learning and conducted himself with purpose.

sentences.zh: 哀帝立爲太子，成帝選喜爲太子庶子。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ai was established as heir apparent, Emperor Cheng selected Xi as palace attendant to the heir.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ai was made crown prince, Emperor Cheng appointed Fu Xi palace attendant to the heir.

sentences.zh: 哀帝初即位，以喜爲衛尉，遷右將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ai first ascended the throne, Xi was made Commandant of the Guard and transferred to General of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ai first took the throne, Fu Xi was made Commandant of the Guard and then General of the Right.

sentences.zh: 是時，王莽爲大司馬，乞骸骨，避帝外家。

translations.literal: At this time Wang Mang was Grand Marshal, begged for his old bones, and withdrew to avoid the emperor's consort kin.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wang Mang served as Grand Marshal but asked to retire in order to step aside before the new emperor's maternal relatives.

sentences.zh: 上既聽莽退，眾庶歸望於喜。

translations.literal: Once the sovereign had heard Mang withdraw, the multitude turned their hopes to Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Once the emperor accepted Wang Mang's retirement, public expectation turned to Fu Xi.

sentences.zh: 喜從弟孔鄉侯晏親與喜等，而女爲皇后。

translations.literal: Xi's younger cousin Kongxiang Marquis Yan was close with Xi and the others, and his daughter was empress.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xi's cousin, Marquis of Kongxiang Fu Yan, was close to him, and Yan's daughter was empress.

sentences.zh: 又帝舅陽安侯丁明，皆親以外屬封。

translations.literal: Moreover the emperor's maternal uncle Yang'an Marquis Ding Ming—all were close and enfeoffed as outer kin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's maternal uncle, Marquis of Yang'an Ding Ming, was likewise enfeoffed as a close maternal relative.

sentences.zh: 喜執謙稱疾。

translations.literal: Xi held to humility and claimed illness.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xi, insisting on humility, pleaded illness.

sentences.zh: 傅太后始與政事，喜數諫之，由是傅太后不欲令喜輔政。

translations.literal: The Fu empress dowager began to join in government affairs; Xi repeatedly remonstrated with her; for this reason the Fu empress dowager did not wish to have Xi assist in government.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Empress Dowager Fu began to intervene in government, Fu Xi repeatedly remonstrated with her, and she therefore did not want him in power.

sentences.zh: 上於是用左將軍師丹代王莽爲大司馬，賜喜黃金百斤、上將軍印綬，以光祿大夫養病。

translations.literal: The sovereign thereupon used General of the Left Shi Dan to replace Wang Mang as Grand Marshal; he bestowed on Xi one hundred jin of gold and the seal and ribbon of the Upper General, and had him nurse illness as Grand Master of the Household.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then replaced Wang Mang with General of the Left Shi Dan as Grand Marshal, gave Fu Xi one hundred jin of gold and the seal and sash of Upper General, and allowed him to convalesce with the rank of Grand Master of the Household.

sentences.zh: 大司空何武、尚書令唐林皆上書言：「喜行義修潔，忠誠憂國，內輔之臣也，今以寢病，一旦遣歸，眾庶失望，皆曰傅氏賢子，以論議不合於定陶太后故退，百寮莫不為國恨之。

translations.literal: Grand Minister of Works He Wu and secretary director Tang Lin both submitted memorials saying: 'Xi in conduct and righteousness is cultivated and pure, loyal and sincere, worrying for the state; he is a minister of inner assistance; now because of lying illness, in one morning sent back, the multitude will be disappointed; all will say the Fu family's worthy son, because discussions did not accord with the Dowager of Dingtao therefore retired; the hundred officials none do not for the state resent it.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Minister of Works He Wu and Secretary Director Tang Lin jointly wrote: 'Fu Xi is upright, scrupulous, and devoted to the state—exactly the kind of man who should stand at the emperor's side. To dismiss him overnight on grounds of illness will disappoint the empire. People will say the worthy son of the Fu clan was cashiered because he would not trim his opinions to suit the Dowager of Dingtao, and every official will feel the dynasty has wronged itself.

sentences.zh: 忠臣，社稷之衛，魯以季友治亂，楚以子玉輕重，魏以無忌折衝，項以范增存亡。

translations.literal: Loyal ministers are the bulwark of altars of soil and grain; Lu by Jiyou ordered chaos; Chu by Ziyu had weight light or heavy; Wei by Wuji repelled the enemy; Xiang by Fan Zeng existed or perished.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal ministers are what defend the altars of state: Lu rose or fell with Jiyou, Chu with Ziyu, Wei with Lord Xinling, and Xiang Yu with Fan Zeng.

sentences.zh: 故楚跨有南土，帶甲百萬，鄰國不以為難，子玉為將，則文公側席而坐，及其死也，君臣相慶。

translations.literal: Therefore Chu straddled and possessed the southern lands, belt-armor a million; neighboring states did not regard it as difficult; when Ziyu was general, then Duke Wen sat sideways on the mat; when he died, ruler and ministers mutually rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Chu commanded the south with a million armored men, yet its neighbors did not fear it—until Ziyu took command, when Duke Wen of Jin could not sit at ease. The moment Ziyu died, ruler and ministers across the river celebrated.

sentences.zh: 百萬之眾，不如一賢，故秦行千金以間廉頗，漢散萬金以疏亞父。

translations.literal: A host of a million is not equal to one worthy; therefore Qin employed a thousand pounds of gold to alienate Lian Po, and Han scattered ten thousand pounds of gold to separate the Sire Ya.
translations.idiomatic: A million soldiers count for less than one wise counselor—hence Qin spent a thousand in gold to drive a wedge beside Lian Po, and Han poured out ten thousand to estrange Fan Zeng from his lord.

sentences.zh: 喜立於朝，陛下之光輝，傅氏之廢興也。」

translations.literal: Xi standing at court is Your Majesty's glory and brightness, and the Fu family's ruin or rise.'
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xi's presence at court is both your majesty's good fortune and the making or breaking of the Fu clan.'

sentences.zh: 上亦自重之。

translations.literal: The sovereign also on his own valued him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor himself still set great store by him.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，乃徙師丹為大司空，而拜喜為大司馬，封高武侯。

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year, Shi Dan was transferred to the office of grand minister of works, and Xi was appointed grand marshal and enfeoffed as Marquis of Gaowu.
translations.idiomatic: The following first month the emperor moved Shi Dan into the grand minister of works post, appointed Fu Xi grand marshal, and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Gaowu.

sentences.zh: 丁、傅驕奢，皆嫉喜之恭儉。

translations.literal: The Ding and Fu clans were arrogant and extravagant; they all resented Xi's respectfulness and frugality.
translations.idiomatic: The Ding and Fu clans lived in swaggering luxury and all resented Fu Xi's modest restraint.

sentences.zh: 又傅太后欲求稱尊號，與成帝母齊尊，喜與丞相孔光、大司空師丹共執正議。

translations.literal: Moreover the Fu empress dowager wished to seek to be called with an honored title, equal in honor with Emperor Cheng's mother; Xi together with Chancellor Kong Guang and Grand Minister of Works Shi Dan jointly upheld correct deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Empress Dowager Fu demanded a title equal to Emperor Cheng's mother, Fu Xi stood with Chancellor Kong Guang and Grand Minister of Works Shi Dan on the side of precedent.

sentences.zh: 傅太后大怒，上不得已，先免師丹以感動喜，喜終不順。

translations.literal: The Fu empress dowager was greatly angry; the sovereign had no choice; first he dismissed Shi Dan in order to move Xi; Xi in the end did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: The grand empress dowager raged. Cornered, the emperor first dismissed Shi Dan, hoping to intimidate Fu Xi into yielding; Fu Xi still refused to bend.

sentences.zh: 後數月，遂策免喜曰：「君輔政出入三年，未有昭然匡朕不逮，而本朝大臣遂其奸心，咎由君焉。

translations.literal: After several months, then by edict he dismissed Xi, saying: 'Lord, in assisting government going in and out three years, there has not been clear correction of Our not reaching, while ministers of this court have accomplished their treacherous hearts—the fault is from the lord.
translations.idiomatic: Months later an edict stripped him of office: 'You have held power for three years without once plainly correcting my shortcomings, while intriguers in this court have had their way. The blame rests with you.

sentences.zh: 其上大司馬印綬，就第。」

translations.literal: Present the grand marshal's seal and ribbon; go to your mansion.'
translations.idiomatic: Surrender the grand marshal's seal and sash and retire to your estate.'

sentences.zh: 傅太后又自詔丞相、御史曰：「高武侯喜無功而封，內懷不忠，附下罔上，與故大司空丹同心背畔，放命圮族，虧損德化，罪惡雖在赦前，不宜奉朝請，其遣就國。」

translations.literal: The Fu empress dowager again herself issued an edict the chancellor and imperial secretary, saying: 'Gaowu Marquis Xi was enfeoffed without merit; within he harbors disloyalty, attaches to those below and deceives those above; with the former grand minister of works Dan of one mind he turned his back and rebelled; he abandoned commands and ruined the clan; he damaged and diminished virtuous transformation; although crimes and evils were before the amnesty, it is not fitting that he attend court audience; let him be sent to his state.'
translations.idiomatic: Grand Empress Dowager Fu then issued her own order to the chancellor and censor: 'Marquis of Gaowu Fu Xi received a fief without merit. In his heart he is disloyal: he panders to factions below while misleading the throne, and he conspired with the former grand minister of works Shi Dan in mutinous defiance. Such conduct tears down the moral order. Even though his offenses predate the last amnesty, he must not continue at court; send him back to his fief.'

sentences.zh: 後又欲奪喜侯，上亦不聽。

translations.literal: Later she again wished to strip Xi of his marquisate; the sovereign also did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: She later tried to strip him of his title as well, but the emperor would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 喜在國三歲余，哀帝崩，平帝即位，王莽用事，免傅氏宮爵歸故郡，晏將妻子徙合浦。

translations.literal: Xi was in his state more than three years; Emperor Ai died; Emperor Ping ascended the throne; Wang Mang handled affairs; the Fu clan's palace ranks were dismissed and they returned to their old commanderies; Yan led wife and children and moved to Hepu.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xi spent three years in his fief. After Emperor Ai died and the child Emperor Ping ascended, Wang Mang took charge, stripped the Fu clan of their titles, and sent them home; Fu Yan removed his wife and children to Hepu on the southern coast.

sentences.zh: 莽白太后下詔曰：「高武侯喜姿性端愨，論議忠直。

translations.literal: Mang informed the empress dowager and issued an edict saying: 'Gaowu Marquis Xi in bearing and nature is upright and careful; in discussion and deliberation loyal and straight.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mang persuaded the empress dowager to issue an edict: 'Marquis of Gaowu Fu Xi is sober, steady, and outspoken in loyalty.

sentences.zh: 雖與故定陶太后有屬，終不順指從邪，介然守節，以故斥逐就國。

translations.literal: Although he had kinship with the former Dowager of Dingtao, in the end he did not follow finger-pointing and follow evil; firmly he guarded integrity; for this reason he was expelled and sent to his state.
translations.idiomatic: Though related to the late Dowager of Dingtao, he never truckled to her whims; he held his integrity and was banished to his fief for it.

sentences.zh: 傳不云乎？

translations.literal: Does the Classic not say?
translations.idiomatic: Does not the Analects say,

sentences.zh: 『歲寒然後知松伯之後凋也』。

translations.literal: 'Only when the year turns cold do we know that the pine and cypress are the last to wither.
translations.idiomatic: 'Only when the cold season comes do we see that the pine and cypress wither last.

sentences.zh: 其還喜長安，以故高安侯莫府賜喜，位特進，奉朝請。」

translations.literal: Let Xi be returned to Chang'an; grant him the former Gao'an Marquis's mansion; rank specially advanced; attend court audience.'
translations.idiomatic: Recall Fu Xi to Chang'an, grant him the former Gao'an Marquis's mansion as a residence, advance him to specially advanced rank, and permit him to attend scheduled audiences.'

sentences.zh: 喜雖外見褒賞，孤立憂懼，後復遣就國，以壽終。

translations.literal: Although Xi outwardly received praise and rewards, he stood alone in worry and fear; later again he was sent to his state, and ended his life by old age.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly honored, Fu Xi lived in isolation and dread, was sent back to his fief a second time, and died there in old age.

sentences.zh: 莽賜謚曰貞侯。

translations.literal: Mang bestowed posthumous name Marquis Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mang gave him the posthumous title Marquis of Integrity.

sentences.zh: 子嗣，莽敗乃絕。

translations.literal: A son succeeded; when Mang was defeated, then it was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: His son inherited the line, which ended when Wang Mang fell.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：自宜、元、成、哀外戚興者，許、史、三王、丁、傅之家，皆重侯累將，窮貴極富，見其位矣，未見其人也。

translations.literal: The appraiser says: From Emperor Xuan, Yuan, Cheng, and Ai, those by whom outer kin rose—the houses of Xu, Shi, the three Wangs, Ding, and Fu—all piled marquisates and repeated generalships, exhausted nobility and exhausted wealth; one sees their positions, one has not seen their persons.
translations.idiomatic: The historian's judgment: From the reigns of Xuan through Ai, the consort clans—the Xu, the Shi, the three Wang lines, the Ding, and the Fu—stacked marquisates and generalships until they towered in wealth and rank; you could see their offices, rarely the men who deserved them.

sentences.zh: 陽平之王多有材能，好事慕名，其勢尤盛，曠貴最久。

translations.literal: The Wangs of Yangping mostly had talent and ability, loved affairs and sought fame; their power was especially flourishing; among them they held noble rank the longest.
translations.idiomatic: The Yangping Wangs were unusually able, ambitious, and conspicuous; no other kin clan held such power for so long.

sentences.zh: 然至於莽，亦以覆國。

translations.literal: Yet reaching to Mang, thereby also overturned the state.
translations.idiomatic: Yet it was that same house that produced Wang Mang and overturned the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 王商有剛毅節，廢黜以憂死，非其罪也。

translations.literal: Wang Shang had firm and resolute integrity; dismissed and demoted, he died of worry; it was not his crime.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shang was a man of iron principle; driven from office, he died of grief for a fault that was not his own.

sentences.zh: 史丹父子相繼，高以重厚，位至三公。

translations.literal: Shi Dan and his father succeeded one another in office; Gao was famed for weighty steadiness, and their rank reached the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Dan and his father Shi Gao followed each other into high office; the father was famed for sober reliability, and both rose to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 丹之輔道副主，掩惡揚美，傅會善意，雖宿儒達士無以加焉。

translations.literal: Dan's assisting and guiding the deputy lord, covering evil and raising beauty, attaching and joining good intentions—even old Confucians and penetrating scholars had nothing by which to add thereto.
translations.idiomatic: In guiding the heir he glossed over faults, magnified virtues, and put the best face on the prince's intentions—skills no veteran scholar could have surpassed.

sentences.zh: 及其歷房闥，入臥內，推至誠，犯顏色，動寤萬乘，轉移大謀，卒成太子，安母后之位。

translations.literal: Reaching to when he passed through the bedchamber doors, entered the inner sleeping quarters, pushed utmost sincerity, violated facial expression, moved and awakened the ten thousand chariots, shifted great plans, in the end completed the heir apparent, secured the empress dowager's position.
translations.idiomatic: When he crossed into the inner apartments, spoke with blunt sincerity, and risked the emperor's anger, he swayed a decision that touched the throne itself, secured the succession for the crown prince, and preserved the empress's station.

sentences.zh: 「無言不讎」，終獲忠貞之報。

translations.literal: 'No word spoken without answer'—in the end he obtained the reward of loyalty and steadfastness.
translations.idiomatic: The ode says, 'No loyal word goes unanswered'—and he lived to see the reward of his constancy.

sentences.zh: 傅喜守節不傾，亦蒙後凋之賞。

translations.literal: Fu Xi guarded integrity and did not lean; also received the reward of later withering.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xi held his integrity without wavering and likewise earned the praise reserved for the last evergreen.

sentences.zh: 哀、平際會，禍福速哉！

translations.literal: At the juncture meeting of Ai and Ping—misfortune and fortune swift!
translations.idiomatic: How swiftly fortune and misfortune alternated at the juncture of the Ai and Ping reigns!
